issues.problem: Results are keyed 'mipnerf360' but the benchmark dataset is 'mipnerf360-pilr'; tools/bench.py summarize looks up paper.datasets[job.dataset] (bench.py:348), so the summary will show no paper numbers and will fall back to the 3DGS-paper reference.
issues.evidence: bench.py:348 pblock = paper['datasets'].get(dataset); only 'mipnerf360' is present
issues.fix: Add a 'mipnerf360-pilr' alias block (same numbers), or pass a pilr-keyed copy to summarize --paper.

issues.problem: bench.py has no per-scene method mapping. A single launch with --methods spec-gaussian spec-gaussian-indoor over garden and counter would train all four combinations.
issues.fix: Use two launches (spec-gaussian on garden, spec-gaussian-indoor on counter) or one exp with --scenes per method.

issues.problem: At 2000 steps c_s is off (spec_start 3000), so the 23.55 vs 23.19 smoke gain tests only abs-grad densification at 0.0005 and spatial_lr_scale 5, not the ASG field. Only the step-500 diagnostic (23.73) exercises the ASG field.

The supp. ablation (w/o c2f 28.01 vs Full 28.18, 3.56M vs 3.10M Gaussians) implies the paper's Full row used c2f, but the released train.py only has the abs-grad half. If the gap is large, the resolution schedule is a likely cause.
issues.evidence: table/ablation-full.tex; git log -S over train.py history shows no resolution schedule
issues.fix: If the 30k result falls short, run the -c2f variants as the documented ablation (labelled paper-text, not tuned).

issues.problem: Abs-grad at 0.0005 already gives 2.1x the baseline Gaussian count at 2k (1.72M vs 0.81M). The garden baseline ends at 4.1M, so the 12M budget may be approached; the paper reports 3.10M on average.
issues.fix: Check the final Gaussian counts against the paper's Num(M) and record them in the report; a run that hits the budget fails loudly (runtime.py).

issues.problem: The official config has a 20-px screen-size prune after 3000 (max_radii2D) and clone/split uses >= threshold; gsplat uses no 2D prune and >. The first is disclosed and matches the baseline.
issues.evidence: train.py size_threshold = 20 if iteration > 3000; gsplat default.py:274 grads > grow_grad2d
issues.fix: None needed beyond the existing disclosure.

issues.problem: K scaling ignores the half-pixel principal-point offset when downscaling; this affects only the non-benchmarked -c2f ablation.

probe_assessment.why: Independent numpy axes and formula; isotropic replacement fails the lambda!=mu anisotropy assertion.
Exact shape list per variant and an independent numpy forward.
Render must equal rasterized clamp(SH+0.5)+c_s, and the gap vs SH-only must exceed 1e-2. It also checks gradient gating at 3000.
Fresh-path render from the blob must equal the live bank both before and after spec_start. A corrupt blob is rejected.
Requires an absolute-gradient strategy at 0.0005; a signed-only renderer fails the absgrad>signed ratio. It does not test W/2 normalisation, which is in gsplat itself (reviewed).
Checks means lr = 5*1.6e-4, linear decoder LR values, and a decoder update per step.
Checks render sizes against the schedule in -c2f variants and constant size otherwise.

fidelity_gaps_confirmed: Code path: README says run_wo_anchor.sh/run_anchor.sh produced the tables. run_wo_anchor.sh uses train.py --is_real --asg_degree 12, with -r 4 for outdoor and -r 2 --is_indoor for indoor, which matches mipnerf360-pilr. Supp psnr-mip360.tex 'Ours' garden 28.07 and counter 30.12 are confirmed (Ours-w anchor counter is coincidentally also 30.12, garden 27.97).
Paper text (N=32, f=24, reflection + <n,-d>, 3x64) vs official real-scene code (N=8, f=12, view dir, 32-wide 2/3 layers): code followed and disclosed
Resolution c2f is absent from train.py in all commits; the benchmarked variant has it off and -c2f variants provide it

White background vs official black; no 20-px screen-size prune; step-then-densify order; SH degree increments at step 1001 vs 1000; random view sampling with replacement. All are runtime-wide or match the baseline.

Schedules verified against official code. spatial_lr_scale = 5 is hard-coded (gaussian_model.py:104,135), and the runtime captures initial_lr after density.initialize, so the rescale persists through the exp decay. f_asg lr is 0.0025 constant with init 0. Decoder Adam eps is 1e-15, with lr linear 0.0025->0.000125 over 30000 (get_linear_noise_func, delay 0); its 0.00025 initial lr is unused because there are no grads before 3001. Densify runs from >500 every 100 until 15000; opacity is reset to 0.01 every 3000 before 15000; prune opacity 0.005; world-size prune 0.1*extent after 3000.

Targets and baseline verified: garden 28.07, counter 30.12; baseline3dgs-mipnerf360-pilr-30000 test garden 27.351, counter 29.033; the paper's 3D-GS row is 27.73/29.12 and the 3DGS paper's is 27.41/28.70.

Eval fidelity verified on GPU: a 300-step garden run with spec_start lowered to 50 gave in-process validation 20.6429 dB and fresh-process ss-evaluate test 20.6429 dB, identical in PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS, with bank.ACTIVE None in eval.
summary: The port reproduces the official real-scene Spec-Gaussian path. The ASG basis and decoder are bit-exact against the official SpecularNetworkReal for both the outdoor and indoor variants. Colour composition, the step-3000 gating, abs-grad densification (gsplat absgrad with W/2 scaling and count normalisation matches the fabsf kernel), and all LR and densify schedules match the official code. The baked-decoder eval path renders exactly as training does. No critical or major issues. The minor items concern bench plumbing (paper_results key, per-scene method mapping), how the smoke test is read (c_s is off at 2k), the paper-text resolution c2f, and the Gaussian budget.
